mechanism_claims.claim_text: CD4-PP interacts with bacterial-mimicking membranes: CD spectra shift toward alpha-helical structure in lyso-PG micelles, SEM shows membrane deformation/blebbing in E. coli and P. aeruginosa, and liposome leakage shows bacterial-membrane selectivity relative to LL-37.
mechanism_claims.limitations: No intracellular target is proven; mechanism is bounded to membrane interaction/deformation/permeabilization evidence.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: CD4-PP prevents new biofilm and dissolves mature biofilm for E. coli/P. aeruginosa conditions and points to curli-positive E. coli biofilm sensitivity.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=28:CD4-PP prevents new biofilm and can dissolve established biofilm

mechanism_claims.limitations: Curli is supported as a biofilm-context target; no purified curli-binding constant is recovered from local material.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: CD4-PP has host immunomodulatory effects in uroepithelial cell models, including CAMP/LL-37 and tight-junction marker responses, with infection-context changes in CAMP, CXCL8/IL-8, claudin-14, and occludin readouts.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=29:CD4-PP has immunomodulatory effects in uninfected uroepithelial cells
source_locator.additional_locator: xml:sec=30:Immunomodulatory effects of CD4-PP during infection

mechanism_claims.limitations: This is host-cell response evidence, not a direct antimicrobial killing mechanism.

quality_controls.detail: Direct mechanism claims list the assay types supporting them.
Membrane and biofilm/host-response conclusions are not promoted to intracellular target inhibition.
